newsitem.title: USA: Hong Kong elections, press freedom worry U.S..
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong elections, press freedom worry U.S..

text.p: The United States is concerned about press freedom and free elections for the local legislature when China takes control of Hong Kong, Richard Boucher, U.S. consul general in the territory, said on Thursday.

He said the United States felt that China was living up to its promises on many aspects of its planned takeover at midnight on June 30, but there were questions about how long a provisional Beijing-backed legislature would remain in control and about the future of a free press in the region.
"We have some important concerns," Boucher said at the National Press Club.

He said Hong Kong's press "has already been limited by self-censorship," for fear of offending China's leadership. "Some editors say privately they fear losing advertising revenue" if they do not toe the line, he added.
Boucher also said that the United States wanted to see free elections for the former British colony's legislature as soon as possible.
He said he hoped China would use the takeover as "an opportunity to show that it lives up to its commitments."
"It is a basically positive picture," he said of China's handling of the takeover, "but we have some serious reservations."
